neighbours.label: a word inside a fixed idiom whose wording is predictable ('as luck would have it', 'let bygones be bygones', 'on our side', 'time on your mind')
fire: As luck would have it, the bus arrived just as we reached the stop.
After years of feuding, the brothers decided to let bygones be bygones.
Sitting in the dark, she had too much time on her hands.
The lawyer smiled and said the facts were on our side.
He tried to trick his rival and got a taste of his own medicine.
When the boss walked in, she was caught red-handed with the cookies.
We will cross that bridge when we come to it.
The new chef really took the bull by the horns on her first day.
quiet: By chance, the bus arrived just as we reached the stop.
After years of feuding, the brothers decided to forgive each other.
Sitting in the dark, she had nothing at all to do.
The lawyer smiled and said the facts supported our case.
He tried to trick his rival and was tricked the same way himself.
When the boss walked in, she was eating the cookies at her desk.
We will deal with that problem when it actually happens.
The new chef handled the problem directly on her first day.

notes: Card: ' your' in 'time on your mind', ' luck' in 'As luck would have it', 'bygones be bygones', ' own' in 'for his own beating', ' our' in 'on our side'. The + pole is 'to the [advantage/detriment] of'. Weak guess; near misses say the same thing literally.
